recipes.title: Ful Medames
recipes.description: Brown fava beans cooked overnight on the lowest flame — Egypt's breakfast, and its Jews' breakfast too.
instructions: Soak the beans 24 hours, changing the water twice. Unsoaked fava will not soften even in five hours.
Cook with the lentils on the lowest possible heat, covered, for 4–5 hours. The lentils collapse and thicken the liquid.
Do not salt until the end — early salt toughens the skins.
Crush about a third with a fork and leave the rest whole.
Mix the garlic, cumin, lemon and salt and fold through.
Pour olive oil generously over and scatter parsley. Serve with baladi bread. Parve.

recipes.title: Ta'amia
recipes.description: Egyptian falafel made from FAVA beans, not chickpeas — green inside, heavy with herbs, and entirely soft.
instructions: Soak the split fava 24 hours and drain well. Do not cook them — cooked beans disintegrate in the oil.
Grind the beans, coriander, dill, spring onion and garlic in a meat grinder or processor to a pale green paste.
The green colour is the sign the herb-to-bean ratio is right. Too brown means too few herbs.
Add the spices and salt and chill at least an hour.
Shape flat discs, dip one side in sesame and flatten slightly.
Fry at 170°C for 4 minutes a side. Serve in pita with tahini and salad. Parve.

recipes.title: Koshari
recipes.description: Rice, lentils, pasta, chickpeas and fried onion in one bowl — four layers and two sauces.
instructions: Deep-fry the onion 20 minutes to a dark, crisp brown. Drain. Keep some of the oil for the rice.
Cook the lentils 20 minutes until soft but not collapsing. Drain.
Cook the rice in the onion oil, and the macaroni separately.
Tomato sauce: fry the garlic, add the crushed tomatoes, vinegar and chilli and cook 20 minutes.
Daqqa (garlic-vinegar sauce): fry crushed garlic for 30 seconds only, then add vinegar and cumin.
Build in a bowl: rice, lentils, macaroni, chickpeas, tomato sauce, daqqa, and fried onion on top. Parve.

recipes.title: Bissara
recipes.description: A green fava purée with dill and coriander — very green, served with olive oil and bread.
instructions: Soak the fava 12 hours and cook 45 minutes until fully collapsed.
Add the herbs and spring onion and cook 5 minutes only — longer and the green turns brown.
Blend completely smooth.
Fry crushed garlic in olive oil for 30 seconds and stir it in.
Add the cumin, lemon and salt and correct.
Served hot and thick, or cold and thicker. Drizzle olive oil over. Parve.

recipes.title: Alexandrian Ful
recipes.description: Cooked ful tossed with tahini, tomato and chilli — the city's version against Cairo's.
instructions: Warm the beans with a little of their cooking liquid.
Whisk the raw tahini with cold water, lemon, garlic and salt until pale and smooth.
Crush half the beans and leave the rest whole.
Fold the tahini in off the heat — boiled tahini seizes into grains.
Add the chopped tomato, chilli and cumin.
Drizzle olive oil and serve hot. Parve — tahini is parve, and so is the dish.

recipes.title: Ful with Eggs
recipes.description: Fava beans tossed with beaten egg and onion — a fifteen-minute breakfast.
instructions: Fry the onion in oil 8 minutes until golden.
Add the cooked beans and crush them partly in the pan.
Add cumin, salt and pepper and cook 3 minutes.
Beat the eggs and pour them in, stirring at once — egg left to sit sets hard at the edges.
Cook 3–4 minutes until the eggs set but stay soft.
Finish with lemon and parsley. Parve.

recipes.title: Ful Nabet — Sprouted Fava
recipes.description: Fava sprouted for three days before cooking — softer, sweeter and easier to digest.
instructions: Soak the beans 12 hours, drain, and leave them in a damp cloth for 3 days at room temperature.
Wet the cloth twice a day. Small sprouts about half a centimetre long appear.
The sprouting softens the bean and cuts two hours off the cooking — it is a technique, not a whim.
Cook 80 minutes in water until completely tender.
Crush partly and add the garlic, cumin, lemon and salt.
Drizzle olive oil and scatter coriander and chilli. Parve.

recipes.title: Eish Baladi
recipes.description: A wholemeal country bread that balloons into a pocket in a scorching oven — "eish" means both bread and life.
instructions: Froth the yeast in warm water 10 minutes.
Add both flours and the salt and knead 10 minutes. Wholemeal dough needs longer kneading.
Rise 1½ hours.
Divide into eight balls, roll in bran and rest another 30 minutes.
Roll into 1 cm thick rounds — thicker than an ordinary pita.
Bake on a stone at 280°C for 6–8 minutes. The pocket forms within seconds. Parve.

recipes.title: Dukkah
recipes.description: A nut, sesame and spice mix that bread is dipped into after olive oil — dry on purpose.
instructions: Roast the hazelnuts at 170°C for 12 minutes and rub in a cloth to remove the skins.
Toast the sesame, coriander and cumin separately in a dry pan — each burns at a different rate.
Cool everything completely before pounding.
Pound in a mortar to a coarse texture, not a powder. Smooth dukkah becomes nut butter the moment the oil releases.
Mix with the dried mint, pepper and salt.
Keep in a sealed jar. Dip bread in olive oil, then in dukkah. Parve.

recipes.title: Egyptian Mesa'aa
recipes.description: Fried aubergine in tomato with chickpeas, with no meat and no béchamel — and served cold.
instructions: Egyptian mesa'aa is not the Greek one: no meat, no béchamel, and it is eaten cold.
Salt the aubergine slices 30 minutes, squeeze and fry until golden. Drain on a rack.
Fry the onion, garlic and green pepper 10 minutes.
Add the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes and chickpeas and cook 15 minutes.
Lay the aubergine in a tin and pour the sauce over.
Bake at 190°C for 30 minutes and cool completely. Served cold with bread. Parve.

recipes.title: Mulukhiyah with Chicken
recipes.description: Finely chopped green leaves in chicken broth, with a taqliya of garlic and coriander poured in boiling at the end.
instructions: Simmer the chicken in water with a whole onion, cardamom and allspice for 50 minutes. Strain and keep the clear broth.
Bring the broth to the boil and add the chopped mulukhiyah.
Cook 5–7 minutes only, uncovered. Longer, or with a lid, and the leaves sink and the soup separates.
Make the taqliya: fry the crushed garlic in hot oil until golden and fragrant, not brown, then add the dried coriander.
Pour the boiling taqliya into the pot. It will hiss — that hiss is the sign you did it right.
Serve at once over rice, with the chicken pieces alongside. Meat.

recipes.title: Mulukhiyah with Beef
recipes.description: The same leaves on a beef broth — darker, heavier, and the winter one.
instructions: Boil the beef and skim carefully — a mulukhiyah broth must run clear or the green looks muddy.
Cook 90 minutes with a whole onion and bay. Strain.
Bring the broth to the boil, add the mulukhiyah and cook 6 minutes uncovered.
Fry the garlic and dried coriander in oil and pour it in boiling.
Correct the salt. Do not stir much — stirring breaks the texture.
Serve with lemon wedges and white rice. Meat.

recipes.title: Fattah
recipes.description: Three layers — toasted bread, rice and meat — under a garlic and vinegar sauce poured over everything.
instructions: Simmer the beef in water with cardamom and allspice for 2 hours until it falls apart. Keep the broth.
Tear the bread and toast at 200°C for 8 minutes until fully crisp.
Cook the rice in the beef broth.
Garlic sauce: fry crushed garlic in oil for 30 seconds, add the vinegar — it will spit — then the tomato paste and a cup of broth.
Build: toasted bread at the bottom, moisten it with hot broth, rice over, meat on top.
Pour the garlic sauce over everything and serve at once, before the bread softens entirely. Meat.

recipes.title: Stuffed Pigeon
recipes.description: Small pigeons stuffed with freekeh or rice — Egypt's festive dish, and pigeon is a kosher bird.
instructions: Domestic pigeon is a kosher bird — it appears on the permitted list and was eaten in Egypt's communities without halachic doubt.
Rinse the birds well and dry. Rub with salt and lemon inside and out.
Fry the onion, add rinsed freekeh, cardamom and allspice and stir 3 minutes.
Fill each bird two thirds full and close with a pin or thread.
Pack into a pot, add stock to half their height and cook covered 60 minutes.
Move to a 220°C oven for 20 minutes until the skin golds and crisps. Meat.

recipes.title: Alexandrian Liver
recipes.description: Beef liver in thin strips with a great deal of garlic and chilli — very hot, and eaten in a baguette.
instructions: Broil the liver over open flame before anything else — a kashrut requirement that comes first.
Cut into very thin strips — the thinness is what makes the fast fry possible.
Heat an iron pan until it is nearly smoking.
Fry the garlic and chillies 40 seconds and add the liver.
Toss 3–4 minutes only over very high heat. Overcooked liver turns grainy.
Finish with cumin, red pepper and lemon. Serve in a baguette or pita. Meat.

recipes.title: Mombar
recipes.description: Casings stuffed with rice and meat, simmered and then fried — crisp outside, soft within.
instructions: The cleaning is most of the work: turn the casing inside out, scrub with coarse flour, salt, vinegar and lemon, and rinse six times until there is no smell.
Mix uncooked rice, ground beef, onion, tomato paste and baharat.
Fill only halfway — the rice swells, and a full casing bursts.
Tie into 15 cm lengths and prick in several places with a needle.
Simmer in water with bay for 60 minutes over low heat.
Drain, dry, and fry to a deep gold. Meat.

recipes.title: Baked Kofta with Potatoes
recipes.description: Meat fingers and potato slices baked together in tomato — the Friday dish.
instructions: Knead the beef with the squeezed onion, parsley, baharat and salt for 4 minutes.
Shape 2 cm thick fingers and sear them in a pan 2 minutes a side.
Fry the potato slices until lightly golden.
Arrange in a tin alternating: kofta, potato, kofta.
Mix the crushed tomato, paste and water and pour to half the height.
Bake covered at 190°C for 40 minutes, then uncovered for 15. Meat.

recipes.title: Egyptian Sogo2
recipes.description: Spiced meat sausages simmered in a hot tomato sauce — fresh, not dried.
instructions: Mix the beef, garlic, red pepper, cumin, coriander and salt and knead 5 minutes.
Chill overnight — the seasoning needs to penetrate and the meat to firm.
Fill the casings and twist into 10 cm sausages. Prick each with a needle.
Brown them in oil in a pan on all sides.
Add the tomato paste, crushed tomatoes and water and cook 25 minutes.
The sauce thickens and reddens. Serve in baladi bread. Meat.

recipes.title: Mesa'aa with Meat
recipes.description: The meat version — aubergine, beef and tomato layered, without béchamel, and served hot.
instructions: Salt the aubergine slices 30 minutes, squeeze and fry until golden.
Fry the onion and green pepper, add the beef and baharat and cook 10 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and crushed tomatoes and cook 15 minutes until thick.
Layer in a tin: aubergine, meat, aubergine, meat.
No béchamel — the Egyptian version does not know it, and that is also what keeps this a meat dish rather than a mixture.
Bake at 190°C for 40 minutes. Served hot, unlike the parve version. Meat.

recipes.title: Torly — Baked Vegetables
recipes.description: Seven vegetables in one tin with tomato and garlic — parve, and on the table for every fast.
instructions: Cut all the vegetables to a similar size — that is what decides whether they finish together.
Toss the firm ones (potato, carrot) in olive oil and roast 20 minutes alone.
Add the aubergine, courgette and beans and toss.
Mix the crushed tomato, garlic, salt and water and pour over.
Bake covered at 190°C for 35 minutes.
Uncover for a final 15 until the edges brown. Parve — hot or at room temperature.

recipes.title: Roz Me'ammar
recipes.description: Rice baked in milk and cream until a golden crust forms — "built rice", the table's dish of honour.
instructions: Rinse the rice and soak 30 minutes. Drain well.
Cook the rice only partly — 10 minutes in water — and drain. It finishes in the milk.
Heat the milk, cream, butter, sugar and salt to the edge of a boil without boiling.
Stir the half-cooked rice through and turn into a greased clay or pyrex dish.
Bake at 180°C for 60–70 minutes, uncovered. The liquid is absorbed and the top crusts.
Ready when the crust is golden-brown and the rice has taken everything. Rest 15 minutes. A dairy dish — it does not follow the mulukhiyah.

recipes.title: Rice with Vermicelli
recipes.description: White rice with fine noodles browned in oil first — every household's everyday rice.
instructions: Rinse the rice four times and soak 20 minutes.
Break the vermicelli into short pieces.
Heat the oil and fry the vermicelli 3–4 minutes to a golden brown, stirring constantly. It burns in seconds if you look away.
Add the drained rice and stir a minute.
Add boiling water and salt, bring to the boil, then lower and cover.
Cook 18 minutes and rest 10 minutes covered. Parve — it suits the mulukhiyah and cheese alike.

recipes.title: Rice with Khalta
recipes.description: Festive rice with raisins, almonds and pine nuts — here in a parve version, without the chicken liver.
instructions: The traditional version includes chicken liver. This one leaves it out so the rice stays parve and can also go to a dairy meal. Anyone wanting it meat adds broiled liver.
Soak the raisins in hot water 15 minutes and drain.
Toast the almonds and pine nuts in oil until golden and set aside.
Fry the onion in the same oil 10 minutes, add the rice, allspice and cardamom and stir 2 minutes.
Add boiling water and salt and cook covered 20 minutes.
Fold in the raisins and nuts and rest 10 minutes. Parve.

recipes.title: Egyptian Stuffed Cabbage
recipes.description: Cabbage rolls as thin as a little finger — the tightness is what sets them apart from every other stuffed cabbage.
instructions: Core the cabbage and lower it into boiling water. Peel the leaves off as they soften.
Cut each leaf into 8 cm wide strips and strip the thick rib.
Mix uncooked rice, beef, tomato paste, dill, salt and baharat.
Use a level teaspoon only and roll as thin as a little finger. A thick roll is the mark of hurried work.
Pack tightly in layers in a pot lined with spare leaves, with garlic between the layers.
Pour in water, lemon and oil, set a plate on top and cook 70 minutes. Meat.

recipes.title: Vine Leaves with Dill
recipes.description: The Egyptian version — dill instead of mint, and lemon instead of pomegranate molasses.
instructions: The difference from the Aleppo yebra is the herbs: there, mint and pomegranate molasses; here, dill and lemon. They are not the same dish.
Blanch the leaves 2 minutes and cool.
Mix uncooked rice, beef, a great deal of dill, parsley, onion and salt.
Roll thin and pack tightly into a lined pot.
Pour in water, lemon juice and oil to cover.
Set a heavy plate on top and cook 70 minutes over low heat. Meat.

recipes.title: Hawawshi
recipes.description: Baladi bread stuffed with spiced meat and baked in a scorching oven until the crust just chars.
instructions: Mix the beef, onion, chilli, parsley, baharat and tomato paste.
Drain the mixture 15 minutes — a wet filling turns the bread to pulp.
Open each bread into a pocket and fill with an even layer.
Brush the outside with oil.
Bake at 250°C for 20–25 minutes on a preheated tray.
The bread crisps and the fat soaks inward. Cut into quarters and serve hot. Meat.

recipes.title: Egyptian Meat Sambousek
recipes.description: Half-moons filled with meat, pine nuts and raisins — sweet-savoury, and built on oil rather than butter.
instructions: Knead the flour, oil, water and salt into a soft dough and chill 40 minutes.
The dough is on oil, not butter — which is what keeps the sambousek meat and not a mixture.
Fry the onion, add the beef, allspice and cinnamon and cook 10 minutes.
Add the pine nuts and raisins and cool completely.
Roll to 3 mm, cut 9 cm circles, fill and crimp with a fork.
Bake at 190°C for 22 minutes, or deep-fry. Meat.

recipes.title: Feteer Meshaltet
recipes.description: A hundred paper-thin buttered layers — "the layered pastry", eaten with honey or cheese.
instructions: Knead the flour, water and salt into a soft dough and rest 40 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls, coat in melted butter and rest another 30 minutes.
Stretch each ball until it is completely transparent and you can see the table through it — that is the whole skill.
Brush with butter and fold into a square. Repeat through all six.
Stack the six squares in a round tin, brushing butter between each layer.
Bake at 220°C for 28–30 minutes until golden and crisp. Dairy — served with honey or cheese.

recipes.title: Eish Shamsi — Sun Bread
recipes.description: A sourdough proved in the sun on a bed of bran — a method thousands of years old, from Upper Egypt.
instructions: Mix the flour, starter, water and salt and knead 12 minutes. The dough will be wet and sticky.
Rise 2 hours, covered.
Divide into balls, roll in bran and set on a wooden board dusted with bran.
Put them in direct sun for 2–3 hours — the heat and light are the prove. Cover with thin cloth against insects.
The dough swells and cracks appear across the surface. That is the sign.
Bake on a stone at 250°C for 12–15 minutes. Parve.

recipes.title: Eish Merahrah
recipes.description: A thin maize bread with fenugreek, baked very flat — its smell is strong and bittersweet.
instructions: Soak the ground fenugreek in hot water 30 minutes — the soak softens the bitterness but leaves the smell, which is the point.
Mix everything into a very wet dough, almost a thick batter.
Rise 2½ hours, covered.
Dust a surface generously with bran and press the dough very thin — 5 mm.
Rest 20 minutes before baking.
Bake on a stone at 260°C for 10–12 minutes. Parve — it keeps a week and hardens well.

recipes.title: Samak Singari
recipes.description: A whole fish baked in salt and spice on a bed of vegetables — the Alexandria method, with no frying and no sauce.
instructions: Clean the fish and cut three deep slashes on each side.
Rub the coarse salt, cumin and garlic into the slashes, not just onto the skin.
Leave 20 minutes. No longer — the salt starts drying the flesh.
Spread tomato and onion across a tin and set the fish on them.
Pour over the olive oil and lemon and bake at 220°C for 25–30 minutes, uncovered.
Scatter fresh coriander to serve. Parve.

recipes.title: Alexandrian Fried Fish
recipes.description: Small whole fish in a flour and cumin coating, deep-fried and eaten with the hands.
instructions: Soak the fish in salted lemon water 20 minutes, rinse and dry thoroughly.
Mix the flour, cumin, turmeric, garlic and salt.
Dust each fish and shake off the excess. A thick coating falls off in the oil.
Heat the oil to 180°C — hot enough that the fish does not absorb.
Fry 4–5 minutes a side, in small batches so the oil does not cool.
Drain on a rack and serve with lemon and tahini. Parve.

recipes.title: Renga — Smoked Herring
recipes.description: Smoked fish split open and served with onion, lemon and oil — all Egypt's Sham el-Nessim dish.
instructions: Sham el-Nessim is an ancient Egyptian spring festival, and Egypt's Jewish communities marked it alongside Passover. Renga is its dish.
Split the smoked fish lengthwise and lift out the spine and large bones.
Soak in cold water for an hour if it is very salty, and dry.
Break into coarse pieces and lay on a flat plate.
Salt the red onion, rest 10 minutes and squeeze.
Scatter the spring onion, red onion and parsley, and pour over the lemon, oil and cumin. Parve.

recipes.title: Egyptian Tahini Salad
recipes.description: Tahini with vinegar as well as lemon — sharper than the Levantine version.
instructions: Mix the raw tahini with half the water. It will seize and look ruined — that is normal; keep going.
Add water gradually until smooth and pale.
Add both vinegar and lemon — that is the difference from the Levantine tahini, and it gives a deeper sharpness.
Add the garlic, cumin and salt and mix.
Rest 20 minutes — it thickens slightly; add more water if needed.
Scatter parsley and drizzle olive oil. Parve — it goes with fish and ful alike.

recipes.title: Salata Baladi
recipes.description: The Egyptian house salad — tomato, cucumber, pepper and onion in large dice, with vinegar.
instructions: Cut the vegetables into 2 cm dice — the Egyptian salad is coarser than the Israeli one, deliberately.
Salt the red onion, rest 10 minutes, then rinse.
Combine the vegetables and parsley in a bowl.
Whisk the vinegar, olive oil, cumin and salt into a dressing.
The vinegar is the marker — an Egyptian salad is sour from vinegar, not from lemon alone.
Dress and serve at once. Parve.

recipes.title: Vinegar-Pickled Aubergine
recipes.description: Aubergine strips in vinegar, garlic and chilli — ready in three days rather than three weeks.
instructions: Cut the aubergines into 1 cm strips.
Blanch 8 minutes only in water with vinegar — they should soften but keep some bite.
Drain and press under a weight for 2 hours to draw out water. The pressing is what stops a watery pickle.
Mix the sliced garlic, chillies, cumin and salt.
Layer aubergine and garlic mixture into a jar.
Pour vinegar and olive oil to cover. Ready in 3 days, refrigerated. Parve.

recipes.title: Fried Aubergine Salad in Vinegar
recipes.description: Fried aubergine cubes steeped in vinegar and garlic — served cold, and better on the second day.
instructions: Salt the aubergine cubes 30 minutes, squeeze and dry.
Deep-fry to a golden brown and drain on a rack.
Mix the crushed garlic, vinegar, cumin and salt.
Pour it over the aubergine while still hot — hot, it absorbs; cold, it is only coated.
Add sliced chilli and parsley.
Chill at least 4 hours. Better on the second day. Parve.

recipes.title: Rocket and Onion Salad
recipes.description: Peppery rocket with onion and lemon — the salad that comes with fried fish, always.
instructions: Wash the rocket in very cold water and dry well — cold, it stays crisp.
Slice the onion as thin as it will go, almost translucent.
Salt the onion, rest 10 minutes, then squeeze and rinse.
Whisk the lemon, olive oil, sumac and salt.
Combine the rocket, onion and cherry tomatoes.
Dress only at serving — rocket in dressing collapses within minutes. Parve.

recipes.title: Zabadi with Cucumber
recipes.description: Yogurt with cucumber, garlic and mint — cool and calming, and only at a dairy meal.
instructions: Zabadi is yogurt — the word says nothing about milk, but the dish is entirely dairy and does not come with a meat mulukhiyah.
Grate the cucumbers and salt them. Rest 20 minutes and squeeze hard — unsqueezed cucumber thins the yogurt to water.
Pound the garlic with salt into a paste.
Mix the yogurt, squeezed cucumber, garlic and dried mint.
Add lemon and correct the salt.
Chill an hour and drizzle olive oil. A dairy dish.

recipes.title: Gebna Beida — Egyptian White Cheese
recipes.description: A salty cheese kept in brine — eaten at breakfast with ful and baladi bread.
instructions: Heat the milk slowly to 85°C, stirring occasionally so it does not catch.
Off the heat, add the lemon juice gradually, stirring gently.
The curds separate from a greenish whey within 5 minutes. Leave 15 minutes untouched.
Strain through cheesecloth and hang for an hour to drain.
Press under a weight for 2 hours into a firm block, and cut into cubes.
Keep in brine (a tablespoon of salt to a cup of water), refrigerated. Scatter nigella to serve. A dairy dish.

recipes.title: Basbousa
recipes.description: A semolina cake in syrup, cut into diamonds with an almond in each — made with oil, so parve.
instructions: The traditional version is built on yogurt and ghee. Here oil and water take their place, so the cake is parve and can follow the mulukhiyah. The flavour shifts a little; the kashrut does not.
Simmer the sugar syrup with lemon 10 minutes and cool completely.
Mix the semolina, coconut, sugar, baking powder, oil and water into a thick paste.
Press into a greased tin and score diamonds before baking. Press an almond into each.
Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes to a deep gold.
Pour the cold syrup over the boiling cake the moment it leaves the oven. Rest an hour. Parve.

recipes.title: Balah el-Sham
recipes.description: "Syrian dates" — fingers of choux dough fried and steeped in syrup, hollow inside and crisp out.
instructions: Make the syrup and cool it completely.
Boil the water and oil, add the flour all at once and beat hard until the paste pulls from the sides.
Cool 10 minutes — egg added to hot paste cooks.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each.
Pipe 6 cm fingers through a star nozzle straight into oil at 160°C only — hotter and the outside browns before the inside puffs.
Fry 8 minutes to golden, and move boiling hot into the cold syrup. Parve.

recipes.title: Belila
recipes.description: Whole wheat berries in cinnamon syrup with nuts — in the parve version, without milk.
instructions: The common Egyptian version is made with milk. This is the water version — parve, and the one served after a meat meal.
Soak the wheat overnight and drain.
Cook in water with the cinnamon stick for 80 minutes until the grains soften and split.
Add the sugar and cook 10 minutes more until the liquid thickens slightly.
Off the heat, add the rose water.
Ladle into bowls and scatter nuts, raisins and coconut. Served hot. Parve.

recipes.title: Ghorayeba
recipes.description: Cookies that dissolve in the mouth, entirely white, with a pistachio in the centre — here on oil rather than ghee.
instructions: The original is made with samna — clarified butter. Here solid coconut oil gives the same crumbling texture and keeps the cookie parve.
Beat the fat with the icing sugar for 8 minutes until white and airy. That is the whole texture.
Add the rose water and fold in the sifted flour with a spoon only.
Chill 30 minutes.
Roll balls, press a pistachio into each and space them apart.
Bake at 150°C only, for 18–20 minutes. They must stay completely white. Parve.

recipes.title: Karkade — Hibiscus Drink
recipes.description: Dried red calyces steeped into a ruby drink — sour, and served hot or cold.
instructions: Rinse the dried flowers in cold water.
For cold: steep in cold water for 12 hours. That is the correct method — it draws the colour without bitterness.
For hot: boil the water with the cinnamon, take off the heat, add the flowers and steep 10 minutes covered.
Never boil the flowers themselves — boiling draws tannins and the drink turns bitter.
Strain and add the sugar while still hot, until fully dissolved.
Add lemon slices. Served scalding in winter or over ice in summer. Parve.

recipes.title: Erk Sous — Liquorice Root Drink
recipes.description: A bittersweet amber drink shaken to a foam at serving — Cairo's street in a glass.
instructions: Mix the ground root with the baking soda — it is what releases the sweetness from the root, and without it the drink is only bitter.
Add half a cup of hot water and work into a paste. Rest 20 minutes.
Turn into doubled cheesecloth, tie it, and steep in 2 litres of cold water for 4 hours.
Squeeze the cloth hard and strain twice — a cloudy drink is not considered a success.
Chill at least 3 hours.
Shake hard before serving — the foam is the marker. Pour over ice. Parve.

recipes.title: Tamr Hindi — Tamarind Drink
recipes.description: Soaked tamarind strained into a brown, sour liquid — the drink that carries Cairo through the heat.
instructions: Soak the tamarind paste in hot water for 30 minutes until fully softened.
Crush it by hand in the water to release the pulp from the seeds.
Strain through a coarse sieve and then through cloth — tamarind carries fibres that are unpleasant to drink.
Add the sugar while still hot and stir until fully dissolved.
Add the rose water and chill at least 4 hours.
Serve over ice. Parve — adjust the sweetness to taste; it should stay mainly sour.

recipes.title: Qamar el-Din
recipes.description: Sheets of dried apricot dissolved into a thick orange nectar — "moon of the faith", served cold.
instructions: Tear the apricot sheets into small pieces — the smaller they are, the faster they dissolve.
Soak in hot water for at least 6 hours, stirring every hour.
Crush by hand or blend into a thick, even liquid.
Strain through a fine sieve for a smooth drink, or leave it coarse for a richer texture.
Add the sugar and rose water and adjust the thickness with water.
Soak the pine nuts and almonds 20 minutes and scatter over. Served very cold. Parve.

recipes.title: Om Ali
recipes.description: Torn baked pastry soaked in milk, cream and nuts — Egypt's most famous dessert.
instructions: Tear the baked pastry into pieces and arrange in a deep dish.
Scatter the nuts, raisins and coconut between the pieces, not only on top — so every mouthful has some.
Heat the milk with the sugar and cinnamon to the edge of a boil, without boiling.
Pour over the pastry and press down lightly so it all soaks. Leave 10 minutes.
Pour the cream over in an even layer.
Bake at 200°C for 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling. Serve hot. Dairy.

recipes.title: Cheese Konafa
recipes.description: Crisp kadaif strands around melting cheese in syrup — the contrast between salt and sweet is the dish.
instructions: Simmer the syrup with lemon 12 minutes, add the rose water and cool completely.
Soak the cheese in water for 2 hours with three changes if it is salty. Cheese that is too salty destroys the balance.
Crumble the kadaif by hand and work the melted butter through until every strand is coated.
Press half into a tin, scatter the shredded cheese, and cover with the other half. Press down hard.
Bake at 190°C for 35–40 minutes until the base is golden-brown.
